Most of what I checked holds up, but the register is not clean: 5 major and 13 minor problems. In roughly 150 checks, nearly every number, file:line, lever default and count traces correctly. The tree counts match (141 entry points, 19 of 25 wires, 262 levers, 23 deferred). The paired t values, WORLD endpoints, tag numbers and gate arithmetic recompute exactly from the cited scripts and results.

Major:
1. 02-R11 / §8 Stage 1.7: 'repair ban1 now' rests on an unverified old-tree issue (P1-C3). The new tree already applies hold_out; FAB.contribution is simply unbuilt and needs NEW-03's logits_fn from Stage 3.2, so Stage 1.7 comes before its own prerequisite.
2. §1 and §2 say irreversible closures go to the owner, but §3.3 raises only the wires (O15). The position-table door (C43 / NEW-13) and the 8 kHz grid (03b-16.13) are decided without an owner item.
3. The blocking-2 phase-traversal fix resizes only E1, the WORLD re-run and the U-series. E2-E6 share the 20 MB / 20k-window shape that never leaves phase 1, yet E2 decides 04-Q6 and 04-Q7 on faded-area gaps, and E4 reads worst-area retention.
4. 04-Q10 says the best anchor is live only when CKPT_BEST_KEEP > 0. In code, 0 already means a single rotating global .best.
5. O2's ε = 0.05 is justified as the toy's minimum detectable effect, but that figure is for the six-area mean. Per area it is 0.07-0.18.

Minor: stale or omitted caveats (the 6.8% bytes-per-window rise is an estimate; nested codec at 64 clips; anchor 5 of 6 confounded; 'only ρ is regulated' predates the relative cap R-1); act and resume costs priced at the rejected 20 MB shape; fab.cap missing from the MAY_WIDEN list; the '5% fewer training bytes' misread; '305 → 306 levers' against 262 in the tree; the S0b CPU seed-0 evidence sits outside dec/ and is not in Appendix C; LM.anchor_term cited for a different job; the interim 'replay' flip changes every default run and has no owner item; the O6 'downgrade' framing; a WORLD command that trips the script's ran-out-of-stream flag; small wording and path ambiguities.

checks.summary:
I made about 190 checks across §3-§8 and the appendices. Nearly all of it holds: the tree cites, the lever defaults, and the counts (141 entry points, 19 of 25 wires, 262 levers, 23 deferred). The WORLD, S0b and toy numbers reproduce from results/ and from the scratch scripts I re-ran, and the arithmetic checks out.

Five major problems:
1. **03b-16.22 (line 373).** The row says the built resume record grows ~10 bytes per position (~26 MB per run). What c8d8e33 actually saves is a small event log: one entry at the epoch's start plus one per act. The 26 MB is 03b's design estimate.
2. **SIG-width trigger.** Lines 635 and 905 say it "has fired". Lines 249 and 384 hedge instead, and the measured whole-tail drift is +4.2%, below the 5% trigger.
3. **Held-out combinations (note 03-16.4, C23, §7.1 row 3).** The design-world readings are called uninformative because of "6-12 prompts per combination". They were actually scored on 200 prompts; the 6-12 figure belongs to 03b's live-codec prototypes. So 0.94 in-distribution against 0.03 on held-out combinations is real evidence against form 3.
4. **04-6.2 (line 473).** The shipped probe cadence of 1000 gives only 4 readings in phase 1, not 5, so it fails the ruling's own floor of 5 per phase. At k1000 two phases get 4.
5. **`DATA_SRC_CAP`.** It is defined per source per phase in 04-Q12, but its owner-set value (O18, Appendix B) is per origin per session.

Ten minor problems: a stale P1-C3 cite left in C37, a D2 paraphrase shown as a quote in O9, arithmetic that ignores the 1000-step warmup, a percentage range quoted for the wrong area count in C04, one wrong section cite, and dropped seed or pairing caveats.
